codeReview.summary: Implementation fully covers all expected behaviors. Four shared story files (Button, Card, Input, Checkbox) import exclusively from @platform/ui public package exports — no deep imports or app-local dependencies. Preview config loads shared global CSS via @platform/ui/styles and implements theme switching through a decorator that toggles the dark class on document.documentElement. All stories use tags: ["autodocs"] for automatic docs pages, @storybook/addon-docs is installed and configured, and @storybook/addon-a11y provides the a11y review surface. Two interaction play tests (Button ClickInteraction, Input TypeInteraction) exercise Storybook's testing surface using storybook/test utilities (userEvent, expect, within). Code quality is high: idiomatic meta satisfies Meta<typeof Component> pattern, proper fn() mock usage, clean testing-library patterns in play functions. The react-docgen switch from react-docgen-typescript is a reasonable tradeoff for Storybook 9 compatibility (documented in handoff as a discovered issue).

issues.description: The theme decorator calls Story() as a function rather than rendering <Story /> as JSX. While this works in Storybook 9's react-vite framework, the JSX form (<Story />) is the more conventional and documented pattern. Functionally equivalent here but worth noting for consistency with Storybook documentation examples.

reactDocgen was switched from react-docgen-typescript to react-docgen. This causes CVA VariantProps intersection types to show as 'unknown' in the ArgTypes table for variant and size props. Acceptable tradeoff for Storybook 9 compatibility, but richer prop docs could be achieved in the future with explicit JSDoc annotations or standalone prop interfaces.

summary: Clean pass. All four expected behaviors are fully met: stories import from @platform/ui public exports, preview loads shared global CSS with working light/dark theme switching, docs/autodocs and a11y surfaces are configured and verified, and two interaction play tests (Button click, Input type) exercise the testing surface. The commit is well-scoped (7 files, 230 insertions), all verification commands passed (lint, typecheck, build), and interactive checks confirmed the full Storybook surface including docs pages with ArgTypes, a11y with 0 violations, interaction tab with passing assertions, and theme toggle changing root class and component appearance. Two non-blocking issues noted: Story() function call vs JSX convention in decorator, and react-docgen type resolution limitation for CVA props.
